title: Space records and cosmic explosions

slides.headline: Space records and cosmic explosions
slides.subtitle: Catch up on this week's most interesting science news in five quick slides.

slides.headline: SpaceX sets a quick-launch record
slides.explanation: SpaceX successfully launched two Falcon 9 rockets just 38 minutes apart on Saturday. This feat highlights how rapidly the company is scaling its launch capabilities for space missions.

slides.headline: Fighting a massive wildfire in Belgium
slides.explanation: Firefighters, water-bombing aircraft, and local farmers are working together to stop a huge wildfire near the German border. It is the largest fire of its kind in the region's modern history.

slides.headline: A historic glide in aviation history
slides.explanation: On August 16, 1963, NASA tested the M2-F1 prototype by completing its very first glide flight. This wingless aircraft paved the way for future designs in space flight engineering.

slides.headline: How islands shape beetle evolution
slides.explanation: Researchers found that flightless beetles on Japan's largest island evolved unique body shapes to hunt snails. It shows how geographic isolation can drive species to adapt in unexpected ways.

slides.headline: A black hole's violent meal
slides.explanation: Astronomers watched a black hole shred a massive star, releasing 400 billion times the energy of our sun. The sheer power of this event offers a rare look at how black holes interact with their surroundings.

caption:
From record-breaking rocket launches to the evolution of beetles on islands, science is moving fast this week.
